about.title: Arcata Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Arcata is a small city, and a fatal traffic collision here touches the whole community. Humboldt County recorded one traffic death alongside 37 injury collisions in the most recent reporting year, on corridors residents drive daily, including Samoa Boulevard, Alliance Road, 11th Street, and H Street. Behind every number is a family facing funeral arrangements, lost income, and a future that looks nothing like they planned. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, children, and certain other dependents the right to pursue a wrongful death claim, but that right comes with a strict two-year deadline from the date of death, and an even shorter window if a government entity may be responsible. Our team handles wrongful death claims in Arcata and can explain your options and handle the legal work while your family focuses on healing.

whyChoose.title: What Families in Arcata Should Understand

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some situations. We can help you understand who has the right to bring a claim in your specific family situation.

items.title: A Firm Two-Year Deadline Applies
items.desc: California generally requires a wrongful death claim to be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government road or agency may be involved. Missing this deadline can end a family's right to recover, so timing matters.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Funeral Costs
items.desc: Damages in a wrongful death claim can include burial and funeral expenses, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and compensation for the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. This is a civil claim, separate from any criminal proceedings connected to the crash.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Arcata?
items.answer: California generally sets a two-year deadline from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a public road agency, may share responsibility, the deadline is much shorter and requires prompt action. We can confirm the exact timeline once we understand the details of your case.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring this claim?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing depending on the circumstances. Because eligibility can get complicated in blended or extended families, it's worth having us review your situation.

items.question: Does the location of the crash on a road like Samoa Boulevard or 11th Street matter for our claim?
items.answer: The specific road doesn't automatically determine liability, but where and how a collision happened can affect what evidence is available and who might be responsible. We are familiar with Humboldt County crash patterns and can help gather police reports, witness information, and other records tied to the location.

items.question: Is this the same as a criminal case against the at-fault driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on compensation for the surviving family, regardless of whether criminal charges are filed. The two processes can move on different timelines and have different outcomes. We can explain how the civil side works alongside any criminal matter.
